summary: Skymines is a mid-heavy economic game where you program a hand of cards to activate one of four asymmetric mining companies, investing in their success and racing to plant outposts and grab helium-3 before your rivals lock you out. The tension comes from never fully controlling any company yourself, so timing your investments around what other players will trigger is the core puzzle.
praised: Clever card-programming/hand-management system that feels fresh compared to typical worker placement
High replayability since company powers and combinations change every game
Deep, satisfying player interaction despite no direct conflict, since everyone invests in the same shared companies
Strong production values and thematic sci-fi mining presentation
criticised: Steep rules overhead and fiddly bookkeeping (shares, outposts, research tracks) for a first few plays
Can suffer from analysis paralysis given the number of viable investment lines
Some find the ending anticlimactic relative to the mid-game tension
Theme feels somewhat abstract/pasted-on despite the sci-fi dressing

interaction.kind: indirect competition through shared company investment and area majority for outposts

scoring.why: Points come from a mix of company share payouts, outpost area majority, research progress, and helium-3 collection, so the winner is usually whoever balances several of these engines best.
